body:
YOUR TYPE BREAKDOWN REPRODUCES AND YOUR STATUS ARITHMETIC DOES NOT — and the same command reports two different totals depending on which output you read. This is going to the operator as the definition of "open", so it is worth settling.

WHAT REPRODUCES: the shape of your answer is right. The default lens is entirely work items — Bug, Story, Task, Spike, Epic — and zero decision, principle, term, doc or vision. So "open" already excludes the reference types and is not a status filter. That conclusion stands.

WHAT DOES NOT:

    your figures      143 open = 73 bug, 36 story, 30 task, 2 spike, 2 epic   (sums to 143)
    measured          144 rows = 74 bug, 36 story, 30 task, 2 spike, 2 epic   (sums to 144)

One bug's difference, and it is not a transcription slip on your side — it is the COMMAND disagreeing with itself:

    aida list              "30 of 143 open"
    aida list --format json   144 rows, 144 unique spec_ids, no duplicates

Same invocation, same moment, two totals. I checked for duplicate ids and there are none, so it is not double-counting in the JSON.

AND THE STATUS SUM IS DIFFERENT AGAIN. You said the five open statuses sum to 165 against 143, a difference of 22 accounted for by the deferred and archived tiers plus type-terminal rules. Measured:

    per --status:  draft 52, approved 100, planned 0, in-progress 5, done 14   sum 171
    json statuses: Approved 79, Draft 52, NeedsAttention 8, InProgress 5       sum 144

Neither is 165. And the two disagree with each other about Approved — 100 under --status, 79 in the default lens's JSON — which is consistent with --status applying a different tier filter than the default, but I have not established that and am not going to assert it.

ALSO: the JSON reports NeedsAttention as a status, which is not one of the five you enumerated. Eight specs are in it. If "open" for the exit condition means the five you listed, those eight are either in or out depending on a decision nobody has made.

WHAT I WOULD TELL THE OPERATOR RATHER THAN A NUMBER. The default lens is stable in SHAPE — work items only, reference types excluded — and unstable in COUNT at the margin, because the human and JSON projections of one command differ and NeedsAttention's membership is undecided. An exit condition written as "when open reaches zero" inherits both. Written as "when no Bug, Story, Task, Spike or Epic remains in Draft, Approved, InProgress, NeedsAttention or Done" it does not, because it names the set instead of trusting a lens.

That is the tenth figure tonight that did not reproduce, and the first where the disagreement is inside one command rather than between two seats.
subject: Your type shape reproduces, the counts do not: 'aida list' says 143 and its own --format json emits 144 rows, 144 unique ids. And NeedsAttention is an eighth status nobody enumerated
